title: improv·artist · improvisational (Jackson Pollock)
mutation_directive: improv artist: improvisational via Jackson Pollock

improv_extras.practice: all-over drip; whole-body rhythm; controlled chaos; no center

v1.feedback: The layered gesture system (umber wash → black enamel → ochre accent) genuinely mirrors Pollock's process and the earth-tone palette is spot-on. However, the fade overlay at opacity 0.0015 works against the accumulation that defines Autumn Rhythm — Pollock's power is in the archaeological density of layers; a refined version should let strokes persist permanently (drop the fadeScene entirely) and instead cap total segment count by retiring the oldest geometry buffer once MAX_SEGS is reached. The splatter dots are a nice authentic touch but at MAX_DOTS=800 they may read as sparse confetti rather than viscous drip impact — double the count and shrink their radii to feel like actual paint contact spatter.

v2.feedback: The Pollock drip-field reads immediately — three archaeological gesture layers (wash, enamel, accent) accumulate with convincing arm-swing pendulum physics, and the Autumn Rhythm earth palette (lamp black, raw umber, ochre, oxide red, burnt sienna) is genuinely restrained. The splatter dots on fast strokes are a nice viscous-impact detail. Two improvements: the orthographic camera and flat z=0 plane make this feel like a 2D canvas demo rather than a contemplative spatial piece — consider a very slight perspective tilt or subtle depth layering between the three process layers so the enamel reads as sitting on top of the wash. Also, the stroke retirement at MAX_STK=80 means early wash layers vanish as the piece runs, undermining the 'permanent accumulation' intent — either raise the cap significantly or freeze completed layers into a merged geometry so the full archaeological record persists.
